1.title: Authentication and Authorization
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Authentication and Authorization. It covers the exam area Domain two: Security. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Implement identity federation (two point one.one). Implement access control with fine-grained permissions, security tokens and M F A (two point one.two). Configure programmatic access (two point one.three). Use presigned U R Ls (two point one.four). Make authenticated calls (two point one.five). Define permissions for I A M principals and resources (two point one.six). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain two: Security (twenty-six percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: IAM in one page
1.text: I A M in one page. Principal. Who is acting: a user, role or service. Identity-based policy. Attached to a user, group or role: what it can do. Resource-based policy. Attached to a resource (S three bucket, S Q S queue, K M S key, Lambda): who may use it. Trust policy. Part of a role: who may assume it. Least privilege. Grant only the actions and resources needed. Explicit deny. A deny always wins over any allow. A role has no long-term credentials; whoever assumes it gets temporary credentials.

1.title: IAM in one page, continued
1.text: I A M in one page. The figure shows this: I A M evaluation: explicit deny, then allows, otherwise implicit deny. Exam tip: Default is deny. Explicit deny beats allow. Cross-account access needs both sides to allow (identity policy and resource policy or trust).

1.title: AWS STS and assuming roles
1.text: A W S S T S and assuming roles. A W S S T S issues temporary security credentials (access key, secret key, session token) that expire. Assume Role. An I A M principal takes a role (including cross-account). Assume Role With Web Identity. A user authenticated by a web identity provider (O I D C) gets a role. Assume Role With S A M L. A user from a sam el identity provider gets a role. M F A can be required in a policy condition (for example, aws Multi Factor Auth Present ) before a sensitive action.

1.title: Amazon Cognito and federation
1.text: Amazon Cognito and federation. User pool. A user directory: sign-up, sign-in, M F A, returns J W T tokens (I D, access, refresh); can federate with social and enterprise identity providers. Identity pool. Exchanges identities (from a user pool or other provider) for temporary A W S credentials to call A W S services directly.

1.title: Amazon Cognito and federation, continued
1.text: Amazon Cognito and federation. The figure shows this: Cognito user pool issues tokens; identity pool exchanges them for temporary A W S credentials. Exam tip: "Users sign in to my app" equals user pool. "App users need A W S credentials to call S three or Dynamo D B" equals identity pool. A P I Gateway can use a Cognito authorizer with a user pool token.

1.title: Amazon Cognito and federation, continued
1.text: Amazon Cognito and federation. Identity federation lets users sign in with an external identity (a corporate directory through sam el, a social login through O I D C) and receive temporary A W S access without creating I A M users.

1.title: Programmatic access and presigned URLs
1.text: Programmatic access and presigned U R Ls. Programmatic access. Access keys for users, roles for compute; named profiles in the config files; never commit keys to code. Authenticated calls. Requests are signed with Sig V four by the S D K using the resolved credentials. A P I Gateway authorizers. I A M, Cognito user pool, or Lambda authorizer (custom logic). Presigned U R L (S three). A U R L that carries a signature so anyone holding it can get or put one object for a limited time, with the permissions of the signer. Cloud Front signed U R Ls and cookies. Time-limited access to private content at the edge. Exam tip: "Let a user upload or download one private object without A W S credentials, for a limited time" equals presigned U R L. Its power ends when it expires or the signer's permission is lost.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A mobile app's users sign in and must then upload files directly to an S three bucket using their own A W S permissions. Which combination fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Cognito user pool for sign-in and a Cognito identity pool for temporary credentials. The user pool authenticates; the identity pool provides temporary credentials.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A backend must let a user download one private S three object for ten minutes. What should it generate? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A presigned U R L with a ten-minute expiry. A presigned U R L grants time-limited access to one object.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An application in account A must use a role in account B. Which A P I call provides temporary credentials? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: sts:Assume Role. Assume Role returns temporary credentials for the role.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A user policy allows s three: but a bucket policy has an explicit deny for that user. What is the result? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Denied. An explicit deny always wins.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A Lambda function needs to call Dynamo D B. What is the best way to grant access? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An execution role with a least-privilege policy. Roles provide temporary credentials and follow least privilege.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Employees must sign in to an A W S-integrated app with the company's sam el directory and receive temporary A W S access. What is this called? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Identity federation. Federation maps external identities to temporary A W S access.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What always wins in I A M policy evaluation? Answer: An explicit deny. Question two. What does a role's trust policy say? Answer: Who may assume the role. Question three. What does a Cognito user pool return? Answer: J W T tokens (I D, access and refresh).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does a Cognito identity pool provide? Answer: Temporary A W S credentials. Question five. Whose permissions does a presigned U R L use? Answer: The signer's. Question six. Which service issues temporary credentials? Answer: A W S S T S.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. I A M: default deny; explicit deny wins; roles for compute; least privilege. S T S: Assume Role, Assume Role With Web Identity, Assume Role With S A M L; temporary credentials. Cognito: user pool equals sign-in and tokens; identity pool equals A W S credentials. Presigned U R L: time-limited access to one object with the signer's permissions.
